subject: Quantimize connector — reference architecture & interoperability test plan
messages:
From: Luke Mercer <luke.mercer@quantimize.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Nambiar <priya.nambiar@quantimize.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantimize + Redwood — request for architecture review and interop test plan

Hi Camila,

Thanks for taking the intro call last week. Quantimize is excited to move toward a partner connector for your hosted inference offering. Before we build an official adapter, our engineering team would like to run a short technical validation with Redwood to confirm:

- Authentication and token exchange patterns (client credentials vs. mTLS)
- Expected request/response shapes for streaming and non-streaming flows
- Throughput/latency targets for 1k/10k concurrent requests
- Failure/fallback semantics and idempotency expectations

Could we schedule a 45-minute architecture review this week? I can bring a reference design and a lightweight smoke test plan that we can run against a Redwood dev endpoint. We have an initial design doc and a diagram I can share.

Attachments: (none yet)

Best,
Luke Mercer
Director, Integrations — Quantimize
L: +1 (415) 555-0187
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Mercer <luke.mercer@quantimize.ai>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantimize + Redwood — request for architecture review and interop test plan

Luke — thanks, happy to set this up. We have availability on Wed 07/22 11:00-11:45 PT or Thu 07/23 14:00-14:45 PT. Which works for you?

To make the session productive, can you please send the reference architecture PDF and a 1-page test plan with the following specifics:

- Endpoint types you need (sync completion, streaming, embeddings, reranking)
- Auth options you can support (client credentials, API key, OAuth, mTLS)
- Expected QPS and large-request payload patterns
- Any compliance-related requirements (PII handling, retention)

We typically run a smoke test against a dedicated dev model instance and capture metrics via the Console tracing hooks — if you can provide sample payloads that will speed the validation.

Thanks — looping in Hiro and Jonas to join the architecture call.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Manager, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
From: Luke Mercer <luke.mercer@quantimize.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Quantimize reference architecture (v1) + smoke test plan

Camila — attached the reference design and a short smoke test plan. Highlights below:

Attachment: quantimize-reference-arch-v1.pdf (diagram + sequence flows)

Summary:
- Connector model: outbound push from Quantimize to Redwood hosted endpoints. Support streaming completions (WS) and non-streaming HTTP/1.1 POST for batch scoring.
- Auth: primary = OAuth 2.0 client credentials; fallback = API key. mTLS is not currently supported in our GA connector but can be scoped as an enterprise option.
- Expected load: 200 QPS steady per tenant, burst to 1,500 qps across a multi-tenant pool. Typical payloads are ~1-2 KB; occasional 20 KB payloads for long-context jobs.
- Idempotency: we include a client-side request_id header. Retries are immediate for transient 5xx with exponential backoff.

Proposed smoke tests (short):
1) Auth and handshake (token issuance + rejection cases)
2) Basic completion (sync) correctness and latency at 50/200 qps
3) Streaming handshake + mid-stream disconnect recovery
4) Large payload (20 KB) end-to-end and KV cache behavior

We can join the call Wed 07/22 11:00 PT. Prio: verify auth, streaming wiring, and a quick latency profile.

Thanks,
Luke
Luke Mercer
Director, Integrations — Quantimize
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quantimize reference architecture (v1) + smoke test plan — tech notes and actions

Forwarding Luke's design + plan. Quick notes for the review and lab work:

- Auth: we should propose OAuth 2.0 client credentials + short-lived tokens (15m) and NY kudos for supporting API keys as fallback. If they need mTLS, we can scope as Dedicated-only.
- Streaming: confirm they implement a standard chunked WebSocket with resume tokens. If not, we'll test fallback to server-sent events.
- Throughput: their burst numbers are high; for the smoke test we'll provision a small dev pool (2x A40) and set up autoscale policies disabled to avoid noisy neighbor variance.
- Observability: add a temporary route with tracing enabled and set TTL for logs = 7 days. We want token-level RTT and per-request cost breakdown during the test.

Action items:
1) Jonas — can you spin up the dev instance and create the dev token route (route id PART-452-dev)?
2) Hiro — please draft a minimal acceptance script for the streaming disconnect/recovery test.
3) I'll coordinate the call and collect test results.

Camila

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Mercer <luke.mercer@quantimize.ai>, Priya Nambiar <priya.nambiar@quantimize.ai>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantimize connector — smoke test results and next steps

Luke / Priya — thanks for joining the run and for the reference materials. We ran the agreed smoke tests against a temporary dev route (PART-452-dev). Summary of results attached (interop-smoke-results-20260724.csv) and notes below: 

Results highlights:
- Auth: client credentials flow succeeded; token TTL 15m worked as expected. Rejection case (invalid secret) returned 401 + clear retry semantics.
- Sync completions: median latency at 50 qps = 78 ms; at 200 qps = 210 ms (95th = 480 ms). No functional correctness regressions observed for our sample prompts.
- Streaming: handshake + resume token worked. We exercised a mid-stream disconnect and the client correctly resumed with no duplication in outputs.
- Large payloads (20 KB): end-to-end latency increased predictably; KV cache warmed as expected after 3 repeated requests. No OOMs on dev pool.

Open items:
1) mTLS: Quantimize indicated this is a potential enterprise feature. If the customer requires mTLS, we'll need a Dedicated deployment path + cert exchange doc.
2) Load shaping: for multi-tenant bursts we should agree an autoscale bump policy or provide a preset burst window.
3) Observability retention: we collected token-level traces for 7 days; if Quantimize wants longer retention we can add a paid observability add-on.

Next steps:
- Camila: prepare a short partner facing next-steps deck (ETA Mon 07/27) summarizing architecture, acceptance criteria, and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated).
- Luke / Priya: confirm if mTLS is a blocked requirement for any existing joint customers.
- Jonas/Hiro: hand off any TODOs from the acceptance script and lock down the Route config into a reproducible template for partner onboarding.

Attachments: interop-smoke-results-20260724.csv

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Senior Manager, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
